title: mandate delivery, version 1
description: The body mandate posts to a webhook action's URL when a proposal has been approved by a person or executed under a mandate. The body is the same on every attempt of a delivery; the time of an attempt is in the Mandate-Timestamp header. Fields may be added within a version, so a receiver ignores fields it does not know. A removed field or a changed meaning is a new version, which a receiver refuses.

deliveryId.description: The id of this delivery, the same on every attempt and equal to the Mandate-Delivery-Id header. Use it to do the work once.

correlationId.description: One value to join logs on across every system: the run id the agent gave when it proposed, otherwise the proposal's id. The agent knows it either way, and several deliveries of one run share it. A run id is chosen by the agent, so this is a label, not an identity: the proposal's id and the agent's id are what identify the work.

createdAt.description: When the delivery was recorded, in the transaction of the decision. RFC 3339, UTC.

action.description: The key of the action, such as tickets.create.

payload.description: What the agent proposed, or what a person edited it to. It fits the action's own payload schema as that schema was when the decision was made.

runId.description: The agent's own id for a chain of work, when it gave one. Left out otherwise.

status.description: approved: a person decided. executed: a mandate allowed it without a person.

decidedBy.description: The person who approved. Left out for an execution.

edited.description: Whether a person changed the title or the payload on approval.

executionBasis.description: What allowed an execution without a person. Left out for an approval.

spentUnits.description: Units spent under the mandate this month before this proposal.

condition.description: The mandate's condition on the payload, which held for it, for the record. Left out when the mandate has none. Do not evaluate it again: check the facts in the payload against your own records.
